body.en: *Biotechnology* deals with techniques of using live organisms or enzymes from organisms to produce products and processes useful to humans. The European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB) defines it as "the integration of natural science and organisms, cells, parts thereof, and molecular analogues for products and services". Modern biotechnology rests on two core techniques: genetic engineering, which alters the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA) and introduces it into host organisms to change their phenotype; and bioprocess engineering, which maintains a sterile (microbial contamination-free) ambience so that only the desired microbe or eukaryotic cell grows in large quantities.

points.en: EFB definition: natural science + organisms, cells, parts, molecular analogues → products and services
Genetic engineering: change and transfer genetic material

narration.en: Biotechnology uses living organisms or their enzymes to make useful products. It rests on two pillars: genetic engineering, which changes DNA and puts it into a host, and bioprocess engineering, which grows only the desired cells in sterile conditions.
narration.kn: ಜೈವಿಕ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನವು ಜೀವಿಗಳನ್ನು ಅಥವಾ ಅವುಗಳ ಕಿಣ್ವಗಳನ್ನು ಬಳಸಿ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಗಳನ್ನು ತಯಾರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದರ ಎರಡು ಆಧಾರಗಳು: DNA ಬದಲಿಸಿ ಆತಿಥೇಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸೇರಿಸುವ ಜೆನೆಟಿಕ್ ಎಂಜಿನಿಯರಿಂಗ್ ಮತ್ತು ನಿರ್ಜಂತುಕ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬೇಕಾದ ಕೋಶಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಬೆಳೆಸುವ ಬಯೋಪ್ರೋಸೆಸ್ ಎಂಜಿನಿಯರಿಂಗ್.

say.en: Genetic engineering: change and transfer genetic material.
Bioprocess engineering: sterile, large-scale culture.
Modern biotechnology stands on two pillars: genetic engineering, which changes genes, and bioprocess engineering, which grows cells in sterile, large cultures.
A plasmid is a small circle of extra-chromosomal DNA. Its origin of replication, ori, is where copying starts, and it also controls the copy number.
In 1972 Cohen and Boyer cut an antibiotic-resistance gene from a Salmonella typhimurium plasmid, joined it to a plasmid and put it into E. coli.
So every GMO is made in three steps: identify the DNA with the desirable gene, introduce it into the host, and maintain it so the host passes it on.

Ligate the fragment into a vector with DNA ligase

body.en: A piece of alien DNA put into an organism usually cannot multiply on its own. It must become part of a chromosome or vector that has an origin of replication (ori), the sequence where replication starts. The *first recombinant DNA* was made in 1972 by Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer: they cut out an antibiotic-resistance gene from a plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium using restriction enzymes ("molecular scissors"), joined it to a plasmid vector with DNA ligase, and transferred it into Escherichia coli, where it was copied many times. Genetically modifying an organism has three basic steps: (i) identification of DNA with desirable genes; (ii) introduction of the identified DNA into the host; (iii) maintenance of the introduced DNA in the host and its transfer to the progeny.

points.en: ori: where replication starts; controls copy number
Cohen and Boyer, 1972: Salmonella typhimurium plasmid gene → E. coli
Three steps: identify → introduce → maintain and pass on

narration.en: Foreign DNA can only multiply if it is linked to an origin of replication. In 1972 Cohen and Boyer cut an antibiotic-resistance gene from a Salmonella plasmid, joined it to a plasmid and multiplied it in E. coli: the first recombinant DNA.

say.kn: ಹೊರಗಿನ DNA ori ಗೆ ಜೋಡಣೆಯಾದಾಗ ಮಾತ್ರ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Next: Restriction enzymes and gel electrophoresis.
say.kn: ಮುಂದೆ: ನಿರ್ಬಂಧಕ ಕಿಣ್ವಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಜೆಲ್ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರೋಫೊರೆಸಿಸ್.
